📚 Today you learned

The Buffett Indicator

Total US stock market cap divided by GDP — Buffett's favorite single gauge of "is the market ahead of the real economy." Right now it's sitting around 235%, versus a long-run average near 165% and a "danger zone" that starts at 190%. Every prior reading this extreme — 2000, 2021 — preceded a multi-year drawdown, though the indicator says nothing about timing; it's stayed elevated for months before. It's a macro dial, not a trade signal: it doesn't tell you to sell NVDA today, it tells you the overall tape has thin margin for error, so momentum trades need tighter stops and faster exits than in a fairly-valued market. You're 100% cash right now, which means this reading currently costs you nothing — it just means don't rush back in just because cash feels idle.

Also today: Shiller CAPE — a cousin metric using 10-year inflation-adjusted average earnings instead of GDP; tends to run even more extreme than the Buffett Indicator in AI-driven markets because it's earnings-based, not economy-based.
